extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), securities compliance officers, and their legal/advisory teams
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluative criteria for SEC-mandated climate-related (GHG) disclosures by registrants, covering which scopes to report, materiality, organizational boundaries, methodology/assumptions, timing, presentation, intensity metrics, offsets, and phased applicability for certain registrant types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational boundaries (proposed alignment with financial statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that a registrant use the same scope of entities, operations, assets, and other holdings within its business organization as those included in, and based upon the same set of accounting principles applicable to, its consolidated financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission proposed this to provide investors a consistent view across financial and GHG disclosures. (This was the proposal language; commenters urged alternatives such as GHG Protocol operational control approaches.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational boundaries (final: disclose method and explain differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule requires a registrant to disclose the method used to determine its organizational boundaries when calculating Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions, and if those boundaries materially differ from the scope of entities and operations in the registrant's consolidated financial statements, provide a brief explanation of the difference in sufficient detail for a reasonable investor to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows flexibility to use approaches (e.g., operational control under the GHG Protocol) so long as the method is disclosed and any material divergence from financial reporting boundaries is explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reasonable estimates with disclosure of assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may use reasonable estimates when disclosing its GHG emissions so long as it describes the assumptions underlying, and its reasons for using, the estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes direct measurement may be impossible in many instances; commenters supported this because emissions reporting often relies on emission factors and location-based data. One commenter said estimates should not be permitted when actual data is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourth-quarter estimate accommodation (proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed permit registrants to use a reasonable estimate of GHG emissions for the fourth fiscal quarter if no actual reported data is reasonably available, together with actual determined data for the first three fiscal quarters, when disclosing emissions for the most recently completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If used, registrant must promptly disclose in a subsequent filing any material difference between the estimate and actual determined fourth-quarter emissions; proposed to address timing difficulties for year-end filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: fiscal year-end reporting and historical periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that a registrant disclose its GHG emissions as of the end of its most recently completed fiscal year in its Exchange Act annual report for that year and in a Securities Act or Exchange Act registration statement filed subsequent to the compliance date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many commenters supported reporting coincident with financial statements to enhance comparability; others recommended later deadlines (e.g., 120 or 180 days after fiscal year-end), separate reports, or prospective-only historical reporting to reduce burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 1 and Scope 2 disclosure requirement (final, materiality- and registrant-type-limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules require disclosure of Scope 1 emissions and/or Scope 2 emissions metrics by large accelerated filers (LAFs) and accelerated filers (AFs) that are not smaller reporting companies (SRCs) or emerging growth companies (EGCs), on a phased-in basis, if such emissions are material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule ties disclosure to traditional materiality under the Federal securities laws; not all registrants are required—only those for which Scope 1 and/or 2 emissions are material and that meet the filer-type criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 3 disclosure (commenter positions and materiality/target linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters were divided: some supported mandatory Scope 3 disclosure for all registrants, others opposed due to data control, reliability, collection costs, and methodological uncertainty. Some recommended Scope 3 only if material or if included in a registrant's GHG emissions reduction target or goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters proposed a quantitative threshold for materiality or safe-harbor accommodations (e.g., PSLRA-like safe harbor) and furnishing vs filing treatment due to inherent uncertainty in estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality standard (traditional securities-law test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant should apply traditional notions of materiality under the Federal securities laws when evaluating whether its Scopes 1 and/or 2 emissions are material: whether a reasonable investor would consider disclosure important to an investment or voting decision or would view omission as having significantly altered the total mix of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality is not determined merely by the amount of emissions; examples include emissions that trigger regulatory burdens (taxes/penalties) or are necessary to assess progress toward disclosed targets or transition plans. Registrants may still incur costs assessing materiality even if no disclosure is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate reporting in CO2e with disaggregation when individually material
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule requires the disclosure of any described scope of emissions to be expressed in the aggregate in terms of CO2-equivalent (CO2e); if any constituent gas is individually material, that gas must be disclosed in disaggregated fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change from proposal (which would have required disaggregation by each constituent gas) intended to reduce burden; disaggregated disclosure for an individually material gas helps investors understand exposure because governments/markets may treat gases differently (e.g., methane).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression in gross terms (exclude offsets)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant required to disclose Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions must disclose those emissions in gross terms by excluding the impact of any purchased or generated offsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of gross emissions enables investors to assess full magnitude of transition risk and the extent of reliance on offsets. Some commenters recommended also disclosing totals both with and without offsets to increase transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of methodology, significant inputs, and significant assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must describe the methodology, significant inputs, and significant assumptions used to calculate the registrant's disclosed GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contextual information helps investors understand and interpret emissions metrics and comparability across registrants. The final rule permits flexibility in how registrants present this information to fit their facts and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable standards and methodological approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters recommended (and the final approach permits) registrants to follow widely used standards such as the GHG Protocol or other climate-related standards (e.g., certain ISO standards) when calculating GHG emissions, provided the registrant discloses the method used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters urged requiring the GHG Protocol to promote comparability; others sought flexibility to use different standards. The final rule permits flexibility but requires disclosure of the method to inform comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG intensity metrics (absolute + intensity; metric choices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal and many commenters supported disclosure of GHG emissions in terms of intensity in addition to absolute emissions (examples: metric tons CO2e per unit of total revenue and per unit of production relevant to the registrant's industry), while allowing registrants flexibility to use other intensity metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intensity metrics help assess emissions efficiency and progress toward goals; commenters differed on which intensity metrics to require—some favored flexibility because per-revenue or per-production metrics may be unworkable or unnecessary for some registrants. TCFD recommends both absolute and intensity metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and phase-in accommodations for SRCs and EGCs
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters supported exempting smaller reporting companies (SRCs) and emerging growth companies (EGCs) from Scope 3 (and in some comments Scopes 1 and 2) reporting; the final rules limit the GHG emissions disclosure requirement to LAFs and AFs that are not SRCs or EGCs and phase in applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued exemptions or longer transition periods reduce burdens on smaller issuers and preserve access to capital; others opposed exemptions because small companies can be exposed to climate risk and because omission could impede larger registrants' ability to measure Scope 3 emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical periods disclosure (to the extent reasonably available)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters supported requiring GHG emissions disclosure for the most recently completed fiscal year and for corresponding historical fiscal years included in the registrant's consolidated financial statements to the extent such historical GHG emissions data is reasonably available; others recommended limiting to the most recent year initially or requiring historical data prospectively only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters proposed various timelines and suggested aligning timelines with other agencies or permitting later submissions to reduce burden. Suggested deadlines included 120 or 180 days post fiscal-year-end or filing in subsequent Form 10-Q/Form 6-K or an amendment.
